_baseBranch: This repo is single-branch: main is the trunk, and there is no develop to absorb a mistake. It is NOT auto-deployed, though — .github/workflows/check.yml is the only workflow and it only tests; shipping is a deliberate `pnpm deploy:player`. A merge here reaches the trunk, not users. (An earlier version of this note said main 'IS production'; that was wrong in the way that matters, and it was the stated reason for a setting below.)
_requireApprovingReview: FALSE on an explicit decision (2026-08-22): the agent merges to the trunk here on green CI alone, without waiting for a review. Name it for what it is — a WEAKER bar than requiring one, because nothing reads the diff but the test suite, and this repo has no staging branch to catch what slips through. Two things bound it: the hardStop list below never self-merges however green, and no merge ships anything by itself — a human still runs the deploy.
_requireApprovingReview_flipBack: Set this back to TRUE the moment the ai-review reviewer starts posting on this repo. It matters more here than in the repos that have a staging branch, because here the trunk is the only place a mistake can be caught before the next deploy. That path runs through github-review's poll backstop, and cannot run through a request-review job in check.yml: this repo is PUBLIC and homelab is PRIVATE, and a public repo cannot call a private repo's reusable workflow. GitHub resolves the callee when it creates the run, before any job-level `if`, so such a job is not merely inert — it fails the whole workflow to load, taking every other job with it. (Tried on 2026-08-22; run 32594747047 completed with zero jobs.) What is actually missing is a `lectoemocion-platform` entry in homelab's personal/agent-review.yml — the registry lists homelab, ordago-apps and cultuvilla only.
_reviewTimeoutMs: Only consulted while requireApprovingReview is true; kept short so the flip back does not also mean a long idle.
_ciPaths: check.yml has an unqualified `pull_request:` trigger and no paths: filter, so every PR runs it.
_hardStop: This repo enforces its architecture invariants through scripts/check-*.mjs, listed in AGENTS.md's 'Every invariant is enforced' table. Weakening a checker is how an invariant dies quietly, so those files never self-merge even when the checker they gut still passes. There are no Firestore/Storage rules files in this repo today; add them here the moment there are.

hardStop.why: proves each checker flags a real violation
